verified.source:
# Keep track of what needs doing.
app Todos
Given
 Todo { title:text trim min=1 max=200 label="Task", done:bool=false label={text="Status",values={true="Done",false="Open"}} } label="Todo"
 policy Todo read=members
 fixture task=Todo {title="Try Can"}
When
 crud Todo by=members fields=title,done label={create="Add task"}
  examples update record=task
   as,changes.done,request.record.version -> record.done
   members,true,1 -> true
   members,true,0 -> error(conflict)
   public,true,1 -> error(forbidden)
Then
 preferences { view:enum(all,open,done)=all label={text="Show",values={all="All",open="Open",done="Done"}} }
 page / title="Todos"
  card "Add a task"
   form Todo.create fields=title display=inline
    input title
  card "Your tasks"
   tabs preferences.view
   list Todo as task where preferences.view==all or (preferences.view==open and not task.done) or (preferences.view==done and task.done) order=-created search=title empty="No tasks here. Add a task or choose another view."
    text row.title,row.done
    edit fields=title,done
    tooltip "Permanently delete this task"
     delete
verified.existing: Then owns components, queries, canonical form/action bindings and finite appearance. Shared UI owns daisyUI themes, layout, settings, validation/errors and interactions. There is no current general CSS/prompt-styling syntax. The prior typed css map is only a proposal.
verified.human: User authorizes repairing empty preferences Settings, is exploring prompt-driven frontend styling, rejects verbatim CSS in Can, asks whether saved nondeterministic styling results make sense, and explicitly chose keep exploring rather than selecting prompt-only versus prompt+typed overrides.

state.comparison: This is an exploratory language design, not delivery evidence. The human wants descriptive styling instead of handwritten CSS, a frontend AI that can style a subtree, and preserved results despite nondeterministic generation. Compare the three designs against equal source clarity, visual capability, reproducibility, regeneration control, review workflow and finite delivery complexity. Existing Then data/authorization/action semantics remain unchanged. The stylist uses static component templates, stable owned hooks and pinned shared themes to generate only scoped presentation CSS; current business values are unnecessary. A named scope is a candidate spelling, not an approved API.

architecture.instructions: Which implementation strategy offers the strongest combined tradeoff for these natural-language style scopes and durable generated results while preserving the current application workflows?

criteria.saved_generation: Perform AI styling explicitly before a normal build, associating a named Then scope with saved CSS and a compact identity/input-digest/recipe/path record. Builds reuse accepted bytes and flag stale or absent output; regeneration creates previewable changes. This adds scope syntax plus bounded artifact management.
criteria.request_generation: Produce styles when serving the first request, then persist and reuse the output. The initial experience may require less authoring ceremony; runtime generation still needs concurrency, admission, latency, cost and version policies and exposes the first result during use.
criteria.design_tool: Use an opt-in frontend design tool to read annotated/separate descriptions and selected static component structure, saving normal committed styles for builds. It avoids a new language construct, but prompt linkage, scope identity and invalidation rely on authoring-tool agreements.
criteria.open: Retain the issue as an open proposal if no offered design meets the common criteria well enough.
